_comment: B3 (ledger, PR 3) — the deny-by-default protected-store write allowlist. Every Firestore-shaped write site under api/ + scripts/ whose collection resolves to a protected store OR cannot be resolved statically MUST have its key here (file::function::method::collection), pinned at its SITE COUNT (review F3a: a new write inside a listed tuple drifts the count and fails CI). Baseline enumerated at PR-3 HEAD, cross-checked against the A46 census. Adding or re-counting a key requires human review of the writer in the same PR; a key with zero matching sites fails stale. Documented resolution limits: see compositionProtectedStoresScan.js header. B3-EXT (PR 4): param-write helper definitions carry collection param:<name>; helper call sites carry method call:<helper>#<paramIndex> with the CALLER-side collection resolution — per-callsite counts, same both-direction ratchet.

_notes_spec1_phase1.api/_utils/mandateCreationService.js::cr: SPEC1 Phase 1 (PR #740). Two tx.set writes in ONE runTransaction — mandates/{mandateId} (the book) + userMeta/{uid} (the transactional active-book claim + escape-hatch flag); count 2. NEITHER is a composition-protected store. Unresolved because the tx.set(ref,…) target is a DocumentReference variable and the scanner does not trace ref-args for transaction-handle writes; making it a literal would require abandoning the atomic §5.2 claim, so it is allowlisted per the guard's human-review rule.
_notes_spec1_phase1.api/_utils/mandateVintage.js::publishVin: SPEC1 Phase 1 (PR #740). One tx.set — archetypeVintages/{codeId}_{hash} (the content-addressed vintage doc) via create-if-absent inside a runTransaction; count 1. NOT a composition-protected store. Unresolved for the same transaction-handle reason; the transaction is what makes publish immutable, so it is allowlisted rather than restructured.

_notes_spec1_phase2.api/_utils/mandateExecution.js::executeD: SPEC1 Phase 2 (PR #745). The §3.5 atomic execution transaction — four keys, each ONE tx.* per revision-disciplined terminal transition. tx.set(decRef,…) writes mandates/{mandateId}/decisions/{decisionId} (the decision receipt); tx.update(mandateRef,…) writes mandates/{mandateId} (portfolio, revision, execState). NEITHER touches a composition-protected store. Unresolved because decRef = mandateRef.collection('decisions').doc(id) and mandateRef is a passed-in DocumentReference (the sweep's query-derived docSnap.ref) — the scanner cannot trace a handle-form ref ARGUMENT to a literal collection, and the atomic §3.5 boundary must not be restructured to inline one.
_notes_spec1_phase2.api/_utils/mandateLease.js::acquireLease: SPEC1 Phase 2 (PR #745). The owner-token lease (§3.1). Each is ONE tx.set(mandateRef,{lease…},{merge}) writing the `lease` FIELD ON mandates/{mandateId} (the book doc — the lease is a field, not a separate collection). NOT a protected store. Unresolved for the same handle-form-ref reason. renewLease has no P2 call site (the handler acquires + releases only) but its definition write is a listed site.
_notes_spec1_phase2.api/_utils/mandateUniverseSnapshot.js::b: SPEC1 Phase 2 (PR #745). ONE tx.set writing the non-protected mandateUpstreamCalls/{date} daily upstream-call counter (Q5). The collection is a literal, but the scanner cannot resolve a tx.set(ref,…) handle-form argument (only callee-base ref.set() chains), and the atomic read-modify-write — which fires the quota alert exactly once at the crossing — must not be dropped; allowlisted per the guard's human-review rule. The sibling ensureUniverseSnapshot / ensureDailySnapshot writes were made RESOLVABLE by inlining their literal collections at the callee-base ref.set(), so they carry NO allowlist entry.
_notes_spec1_phase2.api/cron/mandate-evaluate.js::handler::c: SPEC1 Phase 2 (PR #745). B3-EXT one-hop helper call sites: the handler passes mandateRef (arg index 1 = docSnap.ref from the active-book sweep query) into the lease helpers above. Each is ONE call. The ref is query-derived → resolves to unresolved; the helpers write the non-protected mandates/{id}.lease field stated above.

_notes_spec1_phase3.api/_utils/mandateClosePass.js::closeBoo: SPEC1 Phase 3 (this PR). The §3.6 daily-close transaction — TWO tx.set sites (the deferred-write loop: decisions/{id} expiry receipts + corporateActions/{actionId} logs + CORPORATE_CLOSE receipts; and the dailyRows/{date} row write, whose mandateRef-parameter-rooted chain the scanner cannot resolve even though the collection literal is visible) and one tx.update on the mandate doc (marks/peaks/scoring/health/execState under revision discipline). The atomic reads-before-writes structure must not be restructured to chase a literal. Same class as the Phase 2 executeDecision/writeTerminal entries. Verified targets: mandates/{id}, mandates/{id}/decisions, mandates/{id}/corporateActions, mandates/{id}/dailyRows — none protected. The pendingScoringAppends write (appendScoringWithRetry) resolves via its callee-base literal and needs no entry.
_notes_spec1_phase3.api/cron/mandate-evaluate.js::runCloseSw: SPEC1 Phase 3 (this PR). One-hop helper calls from the close sweep: acquireLease/releaseLease (the lease FIELD on mandates/{id} — the Phase 2 lease entries cover the callee sites) and closeBook (above). The ref argument is the sweep query docSnap.ref — unresolvable statically by design. Verified target: mandates/{id}. Not protected.

_notes_spec1_phase4.api/_utils/mandateRollover.js::rollOneBo: SPEC1 Phase 4 (this PR). The §5.3 atomic per-boundary rollover transaction — TWO tx.set sites (quarterSummaries/{quarterIndex} tenure record + decisions/{openBatchId} the I1 open-batch cancel, dormant under direct transport) and one tx.update on the mandate doc (quarterIndex/quarterKey/quarterStartAt/nextRolloverAt/vintageRef/cadenceTier/managerAgentId, the quarter-lens reset, lastProcessedRolloverKey, revision — under the FR-1 assertCapitalConserved guard). Unresolved: tx.set/tx.update target mandateRef-rooted DocumentReferences (mandateRef.collection('quarterSummaries').doc(…), the sweep's docSnap.ref) — the scanner cannot trace handle-form ref arguments. catchUpBook::call:rollOneBoundary#1 is the B3-EXT one-hop pass of mandateRef into the boundary helper. Verified targets: mandates/{id}, mandates/{id}/quarterSummaries, mandates/{id}/decisions — none protected.
_notes_spec1_phase4.api/_utils/mandateEscape.js::escapeManda: SPEC1 Phase 4 (this PR). The §5.4 single escape transaction — FOUR tx.set sites (the old book's terminal non-scoring quarterSummaries/{i}; the I1 open-batch cancel decisions/{id}; the replacement mandates/{newId} book; and the userMeta/{uid} once-ever flag + active-book pointer, F6-same-transaction) and one tx.update on the old book (status:closed/voided:true/revision/cohort). Unresolved for the same handle-form-ref reason; the atomic §5.4 close+create+claim must not be restructured. Verified targets: mandates/{id} (old+new), mandates/{id}/quarterSummaries, mandates/{id}/decisions, userMeta/{uid} — none protected.
_notes_spec1_phase4.api/cron/mandate-rollover.js::runRollove: SPEC1 Phase 4 (this PR). runRolloverSweep passes the sweep's docSnap.ref into acquireLease/releaseLease (the lease FIELD on mandates/{id}; the Phase 2 mandateLease entries cover the callee sites). Verified target: mandates/{id}, not protected. NOTE: the eval sweep's acquireLease/releaseLease call sites moved from `handler` to the newly-extracted `runEvalSweep` in this PR (a mechanical seam extraction that made the sweeps injectable for the P3-flagged integration harness) — the two `handler::call:*` keys were pruned and re-listed under `runEvalSweep`; the underlying writes and their non-protected target (mandates/{id}.lease) are unchanged. This supersedes the `handler` reference in the _notes_spec1_phase2 block above.

_notes_spec1_phase5.api/_utils/mandateBatchTransport.js (set: SPEC1 Phase 5 (this PR, incl. the adversarial-review fix pass). The batch transport (§3.3). submitMandateBatch: ONE .set creating the mandateBatches/{providerBatchId} bookkeeping doc (collection name is the MANDATE_BATCH_COLLECTION constant — the scanner cannot resolve an identifier; doc id is the provider's batch id) and ONE tx.update per book applying the revision-disciplined open-submission gate to mandates/{id}. markEntry: ONE .set merging an entry's terminal status and/or billed mark into the batch doc. finalizeBatch: a TRANSACTION (review INV-P5-11 — conditioned on the doc still being 'open') with ONE tx.update on the batch doc plus ONE post-txn .set of the per-day I9 stats sample (mandateBatchStats/{date}). harvestOneBatch: ONE .set (the agedOutAt marker, review MONEY-P5-1 deferred-billing) + TWO one-hop calls each to markEntry/finalizeBatch (the age-out lane and the ended lane); harvestOpenBatches passes db into harvestOneBatch (one hop). drainOpenBatches: ONE .set (the drainRequested marker, review SPEC-P5-3) + one call each to markEntry/finalizeBatch. Verified targets: mandateBatches/{id}, mandateBatchStats/{date}, mandates/{id} — NONE is in PROTECTED_COLLECTIONS (composition/agent-forge surface only).
_notes_spec1_phase5.api/_utils/mandateExecution.js::disposeS: SPEC1 Phase 5 (this PR). The result-less terminal disposition (§3.3/I1: expired age-outs incl. the transport-independent in-sweep gate expiry, API-errored failed, provider-canceled, drain rejected_stale) — ONE tx.set writing the terminal decision receipt to mandates/{id}/decisions/{requestId} (the create-if-absent claim; written even when the parent book doc is GONE, review INV-P5-5, so a batch doc can always converge) and TWO tx.update sites on the book: the normal terminal (revision + the shared execStateTerminalPatch: counters, streak, ownership-conditional gate clear; skipped when the book is missing) and the refuter-D2 GATE HEAL on the idempotent path (a gate pointing at an already-terminal request — the ops-restore shape — is cleared under revision discipline instead of re-billing forever). Same transaction-handle class as the Phase 2 executeDecision/writeTerminal entries. Verified targets: mandates/{id} + mandates/{id}/decisions — not protected.
_notes_spec1_phase5.api/cron/mandate-evaluate.js::runEvalSwe: SPEC1 Phase 5 (this PR). B3-EXT one-hop helper call: the eval sweep passes the db (arg 0) into submitMandateBatch after the page loop. The harvest call (harvestOpenBatches) and the in-sweep gate-expiry disposeSubmission call (runBookEval, review C21-P5-2) are ALSO one-hop db passes whose callee write sites are the entries above; the sweep's own per-book stamps ride the pre-existing persistOutcome merge (mandates/{id}, not protected). Verified targets: mandateBatches/{id} + mandateBatchStats/{date} + mandates/{id} — not protected.
_notes_spec1_phase5.api/mandate/drain.js::handler::call:drai: SPEC1 Phase 5 (this PR). B3-EXT one-hop: the founder-gated drain endpoint passes the live db (arg 0) into drainOpenBatches (F26). Callee write sites are the mandateBatchTransport entries above. Founder-only (§7: MANDATE_FOUNDER_CREATE_ENABLED AND allowlisted uid — drain.test.js locks the property). Verified targets: mandateBatches/{id} + mandateBatchStats/{date} + mandates/{id}/decisions + mandates/{id} — not protected.

_notes_lease_ops_r2: R2 tooling (2026-08-16, branch ops/lease-drain-tooling). B3-EXT one-hop helper call sites in api/_utils/compositionLeaseOps.js — the testable layer under scripts/composition/lease-ops.js, the runbook's step-1.9 drain and step-8B purge commands. HUMAN REVIEW: each is ONE call passing `db` at arg index 0, and neither adds a new write SURFACE — they delegate to purgeReleasedProvisionerLeases and resolveStuckProvisionerLease, whose definition-side writes to the protected compositionProvisionerLeases collection are already listed above at their own keys. Unresolved because `db` is a passed-in Firestore handle, which the scanner cannot trace to a literal collection. The drain and list paths carry NO entry: drainProvisionerLeases and listUnreleasedProvisionerLeases perform reads only.
